subject: Recap: Redwood <> LumenAI pilot pricing, unit economics & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Ford <jamie@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Redwood <> LumenAI pilot pricing, unit economics & next steps

Hi Jamie — thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Target workload: chat + instruction generation for customer support automation
- Expected monthly token consumption: 4-8M tokens (spikes to ~12M during campaigns)
- Target price band they mentioned on call: ~$10–$15k/month for initial pilot

Preliminary pricing & unit economics (high level):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): baseline $95 / 1M tokens (includes model and runtime).
  - Example: 6M tokens/month => ~$570/month (token charge) + 5% infra/service premium on invoice.
- Dedicated pilot (1–3 GPUs reserved): effective unit economics drop to $55–$75 / 1M tokens depending on commit and usage profile.
  - Example committed scenario (3-month pilot, 6M avg/month): target ~ $360–$450 / month in token-equivalent pricing; line items differ for reserved capacity vs per-token.

Note on our math: these are blended per-1M-token equivalents combining token compute cost + GPU amortized + caching/efficiency uplift. Marissa (cc'd) has the detailed calc and spreadsheet attached.

Attachments I included: lumenai_estimate_q2.xlsx (invoice-style estimate) and redwood_pricing_calculator.csv (breakdown + toggleable scenarios). Please review the numbers and confirm the monthly token target you expect us to price to — specifically, are you comfortable with using a 6M/month baseline for the pilot, or should we model 4M vs 8M scenarios formally?

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm baseline tokens (we'll regenerate the estimate for 4M/6M/8M).
2) Procurement provides PO template / procurement constraints so we can draft a formal quote and SOW.
3) If pricing shape looks good, we schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra lead to confirm latency/throughput targets.

If helpful, I can produce a short invoice-style PDF with line items for Hosted vs Dedicated so your finance team can review. Looking to get your signal by end of week to hit the May SOW timeline.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — great summary. Quick answers: 
- Baseline tokens: let's plan on 6M/month for the initial estimate (we do expect spikes to ~12M during marketing pushes).
- Budget: our target for the pilot is about $12k/month all-in (including infra). If you're showing $95/1M hosted then that looks far below where we'd expect compute to sit — can you send the invoice-style breakdown and a Dedicated scenario (monthly reserved pricing) so Procurement can ingest.

Procurement, can you share any PO templates or billing constraints? We need the finance review before we can commit to a 3-month pilot.

—Jamie
Head of Product, LumenAI

Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood <> LumenAI pilot pricing, unit economics & next steps

Jamie — thanks for the clarity. I've attached a simple invoice-style estimate for the 4/6/8M scenarios and a Dedicated reserved-capacity scenario in the attached spreadsheet. High-level notes below so Procurement has context: 

Hosted (PAYG) scenario — 6M baseline: 
- Token unit charge: $95 / 1M tokens (covers model & runtime)
- Example invoice line items: token usage, request throughput surcharge (if > 1k rps), support add-on (optional)
- Estimated invoice: ~$570 monthly token charge + estimated $150 infra/throughput fee => ~$720/mo before taxes (for 6M).

Dedicated (pilot) scenario — three-month pilot, reserved capacity: 
- Reserved pool with autoscale buffer. Effective blended $/1M: $65 (assumes 70% utilization).
- Example monthly invoice lines: reserved capacity fee (flat), overage token charges (if spikes), monitoring & ops premium.
- Estimated invoice (6M avg, 70% util): ~$390–$520 / month in blended compute-equivalent; actual invoice will show the reserved capacity line item (~$3.5k–$6k) + a smaller usage/overage line.

I realize the headline numbers here (e.g., $570 hosted vs $12k target) look mismatched to your budget — that likely means your $12k target includes product, support, integration, and premium SLOs, not merely token-level compute. To make the comparison apples-to-apples, we can produce a mock invoice with the following line items: token compute, reserved GPU fee, 24/7 SLA uplift, integration services, and a training/monitoring retainer. That will show how we arrive at your $12k target.

Attaching: lumenai_estimate_q2.xlsx (contains both invoice mockups) and a cleaned pricing CSV. Marissa — feel free to add any notes on assumptions.

Next steps updated: 
- Vanessa to deliver a formal quote + SOW draft once Procurement shares PO template & any legal procurement constraints (net terms, tax, billing address).
- Schedule technical deep-dive with infra lead (please suggest times Thurs-Fri).

Thanks — I'll follow up with a formal quote PDF if Procurement confirms PO path.

Best,
Vanessa

Adding a quick finance note here — I attached a short text file with the assumptions we used to compute the blended $/1M figures. TL;DR:
- Blended unit = (allocated GPU amortization + expected cache uplift + model flop cost) / effective billable tokens.
- We modeled 3 utilization bands: 50%, 70%, 85% — 70% is the conservative mid case we shared.
- Billing terms: Net 30; tax & region-specific fees extra.
- If LumenAI can commit to 12 months we can discuss a -10% volume/commit discount (applies to reserved-capacity lines, not one-off integration fees).

Attaching pricing_calc_notes.txt for your finance team. Happy to hop on a short call to walk the calc.

—Marissa
Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
